question: Evaluate $\begin{vmatrix}2&0&1\\0&3&0\\4&0&-1\end{vmatrix}$ by expanding along the row containing the maximum number of zeros.
explanation:
Selection of the expansion row
The second row contains two zeros, so expansion along this row requires only one nonzero term.
Expansion along the second row
The nonzero element $3$ occupies position $(2,2)$, whose sign is positive. Therefore, $$\begin{vmatrix}2&0&1\\0&3&0\\4&0&-1\end{vmatrix}=3\begin{vmatrix}2&1\\4&-1\end{vmatrix}$$
Evaluation of the minor
We have $$\begin{vmatrix}2&1\\4&-1\end{vmatrix}=(2)(-1)-(1)(4)=-6$$
Final calculation
Hence, the determinant is $$3(-6)=-18$$
